abstract: Maintains microseismic network records, acoustic noise floor assessments, and deep reservoir permeability data
system_message:
You are Reservoir geophysics lead (GEOPHYS). The Reservoir geophysics lead (GEOPHYS) is responsible for maintaining microseismic network records, acoustic noise floor assessments, and deep reservoir permeability data, as well as managing spectral gamma logging across candidate geothermal sites.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains microseismic network records, acoustic noise floor assessments, and deep reservoir permeability data（SEIS）
information_points.content:
GEOPHYS-SEIS-PN8：For Thermal Ridge Sector, the active microseismic monitoring network is installed across the exploration basin perimeter, with a baseline acoustic noise floor of 34 dB measured across the centroid borehole cluster array. The deep reservoir exploration permeability within the primary production reservoir between 2000 m and 3000 m depth is 35.0 mD.
GEOPHYS-SEIS-J7Y：For Pinnacle Fault Graben, the active microseismic monitoring network is installed across the exploration basin perimeter, and the baseline acoustic noise floor measured across the centroid borehole cluster array is 48 dB. In the primary production reservoir between 2000 m and 3000 m depth, the deep reservoir exploration permeability is 35.0 mD.
GEOPHYS-SEIS-IQF：For Solstice Caldera Basin, the active microseismic monitoring network is installed across the exploration basin perimeter, while the baseline acoustic noise floor measured across the centroid borehole cluster array is 28 dB. The deep reservoir exploration permeability within the primary production reservoir between 2000 m and 3000 m depth is 45.0 mD.

information_points.title: Spectral gamma logging（GMMA）
information_points.content:
GEOPHYS-GMMA-NYN：For Pinnacle Fault Graben, spectral gamma logging within the target caprock zone indicates a total borehole natural radioactivity of 70 gAPI.
GEOPHYS-GMMA-94K：For Solstice Caldera Basin, spectral gamma logging within the target caprock zone indicates a total borehole natural radioactivity of 95 gAPI.
GEOPHYS-GMMA-KHY：For Thermal Ridge Sector, spectral gamma logging within the target caprock zone indicates a total borehole natural radioactivity of 45 gAPI.
